And Another on 20 January, 2023
Author: Raj Beer Singh
Bench: Raj Beer Singh
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 88
Case :- Criminal Appeal No. - 8503 of 2022
Appellant :- Vijayi Chauhan @ Vijay Lala Chauhan And 4 Others
Respondent :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Appellant :- A Kumar Srivastava,Hari Narayan Singh
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
1.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the appellants and learned AGA for the State.
None has appeared on behalf ofrespondent No.2. despite service of notice.

2. This appeal has been preferred by the appellants under section 14- A (1) of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (hereinafter referred as SC/ST Act) against the impugned cognizance/summoning order dated 03.08.2022, passed by the learned Special Judge,
(SC/ST (P.A.) Act), Ghazipur, in S.T. No.674 of 2022, Case Crime No.77 of 2022, under Sections 147,
323, 504, 506, 427 IPC and Section 3(2)5A & 3(1)(Da), (Dha) of SC/ST Act, P.S. Dullahpur, District Ghazipur, whereby, the appellants/accused have been summoned for aforesaid offences and also to quash the charge-sheet submitted in aforesaid case.

entities.text: Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. It has been argued by learned counsel for the appellants that the first information report of this case has been lodged by respondent No.2 making false and baseless allegations and that police have not investigated the matter properly and charge-sheet was submitted in a routine manner.

Referring to the site plan, it was submitted that in fact the land of railway is adjoining to the tin shed of Vijayi Chauhan @ Vijay Lala Chauhan And 4 ... vs State Of U.P. And Another on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191511716/
1 respondent No.2 but the respondent No.2 and his family members have made encroachment upon railway land and fixed gate on that land, which was demolished by the Railway Department.

entities.text: Vijayi Chauhan @ Vijay Lala Chauhan And 4 ... vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 suspects that the said structure on encroached land was demolished by the Railway Department on the complaint of appellants and that first information report of this case has been lodged due to that reason.
The appellant No.5 is not named in the first information report.
The injured persons have sustained merely simple injuries and most of the injuries are complaints of pain.
A civil suit is also pending between the family members of appellants and the informant.

Referring to the facts of the matter, it was submitted that no prima facie case is made out against appellants and thus, the impugned cognizance order and the entire proceedings including charge-sheet are liable to be quashed.

4. Learned AGA has opposed the appeal and argued that there are allegations against appellants that on 15.05.2022 at 3.30PM they have abused the informant/respondent No.2 by using caste indicative words and assaulted him and they have assaulted and caused injuries to the son of informant namely, Vinay Kumar.
The version of informant is supported by injury reports of injured.
During investigation the witnesses have also supported the said version.
5. I have considered the rival submissions and perused the record.

6. It is well settled that at the stage of cognizance and at the stage of issuing process to the accused,
the Magistrate has to be satisfied that there is sufficient ground for proceeding.
The court has to consider whether there is sufficient ground for proceeding and not whether there is sufficient ground for conviction.

At the stage of issuing the process to the accused, the Magistrate is not required to record reasons, particularly when the cognizance is being taken on the basis of report filed by the police after investigation, under section 173(2) Cr.P.C.

In case of S.K. Sinha, Chief Enforcement Officer v. Videocon International Limited and Ors. MANU/SC/7011/2008 : (2008) 2 SCC 492, it was held that taking cognizance has no esoteric or mystic significance in criminal law and it connotes that a judicial notice is taken of an offence, after application of mind.

entities.text: S.K. Sinha, Chief Enforcement Officer v. Videocon International Limited and Ors. MANU/SC/7011/2008 : (2008) 2 SCC 492
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Taking of cognizance is thus a condition precedent for holding a valid trial.
In M/s.
India Carat

Pvt. Ltd. Vs.
State of Karnataka

entities.text:
Pvt. Ltd. Vs.
State of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , the Supreme Court has observed that Magistrate can take into account statements of witnesses examined by Police during investigation, take cognizance of offence complained of, order to issue a process to accused.

7. In Mehmood Ul Rehman v. Khazir Mohammad Tunda and others (2015) 12 SCC 420, it was held as under:-
"21.

entities.text: Mehmood Ul Rehman v. Khazir Mohammad Tunda and others (2015) 12 SCC 420
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Under Section 190(1)(b) Cr.P.C, the Magistrate has the advantage of a police report and under Section 190(1)(c) Cr.P.C., he has the information or knowledge of commission of an offence.
But The order of the Magistrate summoning the accused must reflect that he has applied his mind to the facts of the case and the law applicable thereto.
The application of mind has to be indicated by disclosure of mind on the satisfaction.

Considering the duties on the part of the Magistrate for issuance of summons to accused in a complaint case and that there must be sufficient indication as to the application of mind and observing that the Magistrate is not to Vijayi Chauhan @ Vijay Lala Chauhan And 4 ... vs State Of U.P. And Another on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191511716/
2 act as a post office in taking cognizance of the complaint, under Section 190(1)(a)
Cr.P.C., he has only a complaint before him.

entities.text: Vijayi Chauhan @ Vijay Lala Chauhan And 4 ... vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Code hence specifies that "a complaint of facts which constitute such offence".
Therefore, if the complaint, on the face of it, does not disclose the commission of any offence, the Magistrate shall not take cognizance under Section 190(1)(a) Cr.P.C.

The complaint is simply to be rejected."
8.

Thus, in so far as taking cognizance based on the police report is concerned, the Magistrate/ court has the advantage of the charge sheet, statement of witnesses and other evidence collected by the police during the investigation.
For issuance of process against the accused, only it has to be seen whether there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.
At the stage of issuance of process, the Court is not required to weigh the evidentiary value of the materials on record.
The Court must apply its mind to the allegations in the charge sheet and the evidence produced and satisfy itself that there is sufficient ground to proceed against the accused.
The Court is not to examine the merits and demerits of the case and not to determine the adequacy of the evidence for holding the accused guilty.
The Court is also not required to embark upon the possible defence.
Likewise, 'possible defences' need not be taken into consideration at the time of issuing process unless there is an ex- facie defence such as a legal bar or if in law the accused is not liable.

In this connection a reference may also be made to case of Nupur Talwar v. Central Bureau of Investigation and another (2012)11 SCC465.
9.

entities.text: Nupur Talwar v. Central Bureau of Investigation and another (2012)11 SCC465
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant matter, perusal of record shows that the respondent No.2/informant has lodged first information report of this case against appellant Nos.1 to 4 alleging that on 15.05.2022 at 3.30 PM, the accused persons have abused the informant by using caste indicative words and they have assaulted him and that when his son Vinay Kumar tried to save him, he was also assaulted by them and the accused persons have demolished the wall of the premises of informant.
He has supported this version in his statement under Section 161 CrPC.
In the alleged incident, the informant and his son namely Vinay Kumar have sustained injuries.

Perusal of record also shows that during investigation a video of incident was seized, wherein, all the named accused persons along with one more lady, who was identified as Smt. Kismati Devi (appellant No.5), were seen damaging the structure of informant.

It appears that during investigation several witnesses have been examined,
who have supported prosecution version.
The alleged defence of the accused /appellants or the fact that a civil suit was pending between the parties, cannot be considered at this stage.

At this stage,
only it is to be seen whether a prima facie case is made out against appellants or not and the matter is not to be examined meticulously.

In view of allegations made in first information report and material collected during investigation, it cannot be said that there is any illegality or perversity in the impugned summoning order and thus, no case for quashing of the impugned summoning order or charge-sheet is made out and thus, the appeal is liable to be dismissed.
10.

However, considering facts of the matter it is directed that in case appellants appear/ surrender before the Court below within a period of three weeks from today and apply for bail, their bail application shall be considered and decided expeditiously in accordance with settled law.
11. With aforesaid observations the appeal is dismissed.
